label: Heavy going
summary: The world holds at 38, still firmly in the 'Bad' band, as the Gulf war crossed a threshold it had so far avoided. An Iranian missile attack on an air base in Jordan killed two American service members and left a third missing — the first US combat deaths announced since the ceasefire collapsed, bringing the American toll in the war to 16 — and Washington answered with an eighth consecutive night of strikes on Iran. Tehran says 50 people have been killed and more than 500 injured since the bombing began on 6 July, and that a destroyed desalination plant at Jask has cut water to 10,000 people; a deputy foreign minister declared Iran 'no longer implementing' the Islamabad memorandum, formally burying the deal signed only a month ago. The war widened geographically as well, with Iranian missiles hitting a second Kuwaiti power and desalination plant in two days, Bahrain intercepting projectiles and a ballistic missile aimed at a US base in Saudi Arabia. Elsewhere the ledger was the familiar grind: eight Palestinians killed in Gaza City despite a nine-month-old truce that has now claimed 1,144 lives, eight killed and more than 60 wounded by Ukrainian drones striking Russian regions including Moscow's, and an al-Qaeda-linked ambush on a Malian army convoy in the Gao region. Wall Street closed a losing week with the semiconductor index in a bear market, a fire destroyed more than a hundred homes in the Norwegian town of Krokstadelva, and flash floods killed four in Vietnam's Lai Chau province. Against that, a genuinely good Saturday for progress and for sport: India's Skyroot Aerospace put Vikram-1 into orbit on its debut flight, the country's first privately built orbital rocket; Belgium banned imports from Israeli settlements; England beat France 6-4 in the highest-scoring third-place playoff in World Cup history, with Kylian Mbappe setting a single-tournament record of ten goals, and Josh Kerr ran a world-record mile of 3:42.66 in London. The headline matches the rubric formula (37.8) with no editorial adjustment; the war is worse than yesterday, but science and sport were better.

drivers.headline: Two US service members are killed and one is missing after an Iranian missile attack on an air base in Jordan, the US military says, the first American combat deaths announced since the collapse of the ceasefire with Tehran and a toll that brings US fatalities in the war to 16; Washington responds by launching a further round of strikes on Iran

Iran says at least 50 people have been killed and more than 500 injured in US strikes since 6 July as CENTCOM completes an eighth consecutive night of bombing, with a destroyed desalination plant at Jask leaving 10,000 people without water across 20 villages and satellite imagery showing damage inside the Bushehr nuclear plant; a deputy foreign minister declares the Islamabad memorandum effectively suspended, saying 'the US has violated and suspended all its commitments,' while Iranian retaliation hits a second Kuwaiti power and desalination plant in two days, closes Kuwait's airspace, sets off air-raid sirens in Bahrain and sends a ballistic missile at a US base in Saudi Arabia

Israeli artillery and an airstrike kill eight Palestinians in Gaza City in a single day, including a young girl, while the army expands the area it occupies east of Deir al-Balah by moving its boundary markers westward and orders more families to evacuate; Gaza's health ministry says ceasefire violations since October 2025 have now killed 1,144 people and injured 3,703

Eight people are killed and more than 60 wounded by overnight Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian regions, with damage reported in the Moscow region including the city of Elektrostal and a fire at an oil facility, as Kyiv presses its campaign against Russian energy and military infrastructure in the war's fifth year

Al-Qaeda-linked fighters and Tuareg rebels ambush a Malian military convoy in the Gao region, killing and capturing soldiers, in the latest blow to the junta's control of the country's north and a further sign that the Sahel insurgency is widening rather than receding

Wall Street closes out a losing week as the semiconductor rout deepens: the S&P 500 falls 1.02 percent to 7,457, the Nasdaq 1.40 percent to 25,520 and the Dow 0.77 percent to 52,146, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down more than 13 percent in a month as investors question whether AI spending can be sustained and the re-escalation between the US and Iran fuels a risk-off mood; insurers were the bright spot, with Travelers jumping 9 percent on an earnings beat

A huge fire tears through terraced housing in Krokstadelva, in the Norwegian municipality of Drammen, destroying more than a hundred homes and forcing mass evacuations in one of the country's most destructive urban blazes in years

Torrential rain triggers flash floods in Vietnam's northern Lai Chau province, killing four people, leaving four missing and injuring seven, as the monsoon season compounds a week that also saw a deadly landslide in China's Chongqing municipality and record wildfire activity across Minnesota and Canada

India's Skyroot Aerospace successfully launches Vikram-1, the country's first privately built orbital rocket, from Sriharikota, with the four-stage vehicle reaching low Earth orbit on its debut attempt and making India one of only a handful of nations with a private orbital launch capability

Belgium's federal government approves a ban on imports of goods produced in Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories, joining Spain, the Netherlands, Slovenia and Ireland; the EU is Israel's largest trading partner, taking about 30 percent of its exports and 43 billion euros of annual trade, and Palestine's foreign minister calls on other states to 'ensure that illegality is never rewarded'

England beat France 6-4 in the World Cup third-place playoff, the highest-scoring match in the history of that fixture, with Kylian Mbappe becoming the highest-scoring player at a single World Cup on ten goals; on the same day Josh Kerr sets a world record in the mile of 3:42.66 at the London Diamond League meeting, and the Argentina-Spain final awaits on Sunday

The week's positive ledger: measles vaccination has prevented an estimated 19.5 million deaths across Africa since 2000, with coverage rising from 5 percent to 55 percent and cases down 40 percent; renewables generated a record 53.1 percent of UK electricity in the first quarter of 2026, wind alone supplying 29 percent; New York passed 8 gigawatts of installed solar ahead of schedule; and four litters of endangered red wolf pups were born in North Carolina, with 12 to 16 surviving their first months
